_about: A17 OWNER RULINGS (GRADING-JOBS-1 J0, fixed 2026-10-06) as golden cases. SYNTHETIC typed answers, each composed on an existing golden QUESTION (fromItem); answer text is new only where a ruling needs it (a final answer written without its unit, a non-attempt, an immaterial miscopy, a Hinglish answer) and is otherwise copied from a verified case (fromCase). Graded through BOTH entry points with the live request shapes CI-SINGLE (/api/check-solution) and PARITY (/api/grade-worksheet, typed). Each case states what the ruling requires: the marks, the mistake type, the one fixed unit comment, whether the question is charged (trial/paper-pass count = chargeable) and what share of its model call the premium meter records (ruling 5). Scored by lib/score.cjs as `a17_rulings` (a row passes only when EVERY stated expectation holds).
label: SYNTHETIC

rulings.1: A missing or wrong unit on the FINAL answer of a quantity-valued answer costs exactly ½, in Maths AND Science, at most ½ per question, typed presentation (exam technique), never on a pure number. The step comment reads exactly: −½: write the unit (<unit>) with your final answer.
rulings.2: 'Don't know' / blank on ANY question = not attempted: 0 marks, never charged, never a mistake.
rulings.3: Hinglish / mixed language: correct content earns full marks; language is never deducted (the exact CBSE term still is).
rulings.4: An immaterial miscopy (it changes no value used in the working) is not penalised.
rulings.5: The premium usage meter counts only graded questions.

answer.text:
Since ΔABC ~ ΔPQR, AB/PQ = BC/QR = AC/PR
6/PQ = 4/QR = 8/6
PQ = (6 × 6)/8 = 36/8 = 4.5 cm
QR = (4 × 6)/8 = 24/8 = 3 cm
PQ + QR = 4.5 + 3 = 7.5

cases.why: Fully correct, but the FINAL answer 7.5 has no unit (cm). Maths: before A17 no deduction (ruling 6); A17 ruling 1: −½, presentation.

answer.text:
u = −60 cm, f = −30 cm
Lens formula: 1/f = 1/v − 1/u
1/(−30) = 1/v − 1/(−60)
1/v = −1/30 − 1/60 = (−2 − 1)/60 = −3/60 = −1/20
v = −20
The image is formed on the same side of the lens as the object.

cases.why: Fully correct physics, final v = −20 written without its unit (cm): Science, −½ presentation (CBSE's own rule, now with the one fixed comment).
The zeroes of a polynomial are PURE NUMBERS: no unit is owed and nothing may be deducted for one.
A SUBJECTIVE 'Don't know' (a 3-mark proof): not attempted — 0, no mistake type, never charged, never metered (before A17 only an objective question was treated so).
A Science numerical answered 'I don't know': not attempted, never charged, never metered.

answer.text:
A. Snell ka law: light ke ek given colour aur given pair of media ke liye, angle of incidence ke sine aur angle of refraction ke sine ka ratio constant rehta hai: sin i / sin r = constant.
B. Medium 2 ka refractive index medium 1 ke respect mein = medium 1 mein speed of light / medium 2 mein speed of light: n₂₁ = v₁/v₂.

cases.why: A correct answer written in Hinglish, every technical term exact (angle of incidence, angle of refraction, refractive index, speed of light): full marks; language is never deducted.

answer.text:
p(y) = x² + (4/3)x − 4/3. For the zeroes put p(x) = 0.
Multiplying by 3: 3x² + 4x − 4 = 0
3x² + 6x − 2x − 4 = 0
3x(x + 2) − 2(x + 2) = 0
(3x − 2)(x + 2) = 0
∴ x = 2/3 or x = −2
Zeroes are 2/3 and −2.

cases.why: The question's p(x) copied as p(y) on the first line — IMMATERIAL: no value used in the working changes and every step is right. Not silly, no deduction.
